bullets: Medicare open enrollment runs Oct 15 to Dec 7, 2026; scam calls and texts ramp up in this window (FTC/Medicare).

CMS security team: AI lets scammers run friendly real-time scripts, drop accents, and personalize calls with age and health details. Medicare will not call to ask for your number or address. Hang up and call the number on the back of your card.

drafts.body:
SHORT VERSION:

That's what the two best scam blockers I know cost. A family safe word, and one line: "My [son/daughter] told me to hang up."

I ran sound for 20 years and a cloned voice still almost fooled me.

Medicare enrollment calls are coming. Does your family have a safe word yet?

LONGER VERSION:
$0. That's the price of the best scam protection I know, and it fits in one sentence.

Medicare open enrollment runs through December 7, and this is when the calls pick up. The new ones don't sound like scammers. AI lets them sound warm, patient, no accent, and they already know your age.

Three things my family is doing:
1. Medicare doesn't call you asking for your number. If they do, it isn't Medicare.
2. Hang up and call the number on the back of your card.
3. Pick a family safe word. If "your grandson" can't say it, it isn't him.

And one line you're allowed to use on anybody: "My [son/daughter] told me to hang up." Then hang up. You don't owe them polite.

I spent 20 years behind a sound board and a cloned voice still got close with me. It caught me on the room tone, not the voice.

Does your family have a safe word? Send this to your parents.

bullets: California SB 868, the Plug and Play Solar Act, signed in September; California is roughly the 10th state to allow balcony solar.
Cap: 1,200 watts AC per home. Must be UL-certified as a plug-in system and shut off during an outage.
No interconnection agreement, utility approval, or utility fees; a utility can ask for a simple online registration but can't make you wait.
A well-placed 800-watt kit in Southern California might make about 1,000 kWh a year; shaded or north-facing makes much less. A supplement, not a rooftop replacement.

1,200 watts. That's how much solar a California renter can now plug straight into a wall outlet.

It's called balcony solar. Panels on the railing, a plug, done. No roof, no utility approval, no waiting. California is about the 10th state to say yes.

The catch: it's small. A good sunny spot might make around 1,000 kWh a year, a nice chunk off the bill, not the whole bill. The gear has to be certified and shut itself off in an outage.
